LESSON: WRITING 12.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we keep journals and diaries?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify all the components of a personal journal
2. use the correct format to create a personal journal

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 12.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 12.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify all the components of a personal journal

What this means
In this part you learn to identify all the components of a personal journal. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify all the components of a personal journal.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify all the components of a personal journal. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use the correct format to create a personal journal

What this means
In this part you learn to use the correct format to create a personal journal. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the correct format to create a personal journal.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the correct format to create a personal journal. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify all the components of a personal journal)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing to a partner. (skill: use the correct format to create a personal journal)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify all the components of a personal journal.
3. Practise this skill: use the correct format to create a personal journal.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we keep journals and diaries?
2. How do you record important occasions or dates in your life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify all the components of a personal journal.
5. Be able to: use the correct format to create a personal journal.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
